classification.difficultyReason: Model the changed batting average with two variables, eliminate one, solve a quadratic and check feasibility.

inlines.latex: \text{batting average}=\frac{\text{total number of runs scored}}{\text{number of times out}}

inlines.text: . In a season, a cricketer scored 1800 runs. If he had been out on one more occasion, his average would have been three runs less. What is his average?

answer.short:
75 runs.

Introduce the average and number of times out, then eliminate the average to form a quadratic.
answer.worked:
Let $a$ be his batting average and $n$ the number of times he was out.

$$\begin{align*}an&=1800\\(a-3)(n+1)&=1800\\an+a-3n-3&=1800\\a-3n-3&=0\\a&=3n+3\end{align*}$$

Substitute into $an=1800$:

$$\begin{align*}(3n+3)n&=1800\\3n^2+3n-1800&=0\\n^2+n-600&=0\\(n+25)(n-24)&=0\\n&=-25\text{ or }24\end{align*}$$

Reject $n=-25$ because the number of times out must be positive. Thus $n=24$ and $a=\frac{1800}{24}=75$.

Check: one more dismissal gives $\frac{1800}{25}=72$, which is three runs less. His batting average is 75 runs.
